channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Quaest: Lula lidera com 45% contra 37% de Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno
item.description: Lula leads with 45% voting intention against 37% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, according to Quaest poll. The president’s advantage grew from 4 points in June to 8 points now, indicating weakness in Bolsonaro’s campaign, particularly after the Michelle Bolsonaro video controversy. In all four runoff scenarios tested, Lula would be re-elected, with the narrowest margin against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Por que carta de Bolsonaro virou alvo de Moraes enquanto Lula também divulgou cartas da prisão
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes barred Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after the latter’s letter was released, citing risks to institutional order. In 2018, Lula’s letters were disseminated during his presidential campaign while imprisoned, without comparable judicial restrictions. The key distinction lies in context: Bolsonaro faces charges related to an alleged coup attempt, whereas Lula was serving time for passive corruption and money laundering.

item.title: Bolsonaro tem até esta 4ª para esclarecer descumprimento de cautelares
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered Bolsonaro's defense to respond by Wednesday (July 15) regarding a possible breach of precautionary measures after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro shared a letter from the former president on social media, naming him as spokesperson in the 2026 election race. The ruling also suspended Flávio's visits to his father for 90 days and referred the case to the Electoral Prosecutor's Office to investigate premature campaigning. Moraes labeled Flávio a repeat offender in violating court orders.

item.title: Com iminência de novo tarifaço, governo Lula vê pressão sobre eleição
item.description: The Lula government believes a potential new U.S. tariff on Brazilian exports, possibly at 25%, is politically and ideologically motivated to influence Brazil’s 2026 presidential election. It views the move as interference, especially after U.S. courts struck down prior tariffs as illegal and amid an ongoing investigation into practices like Pix. The Planalto argues that Brazil’s technical objections are being ignored, suggesting the tariff serves external interests in Brazil’s domestic electoral contest.

item.title: Dia D das tarifas: EUA chega a decisão sobre tarifaço nesta quarta
item.description: The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) will decide this Wednesday (July 15) whether to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian products, following an investigation launched in July 2025. Despite a U.S. trade surplus, Washington alleging unfair trade practices. The Lula government is preparing for the possibility of tariffs, as negotiations have failed to produce an agreement.

item.title: TSE libera campanha do governo Lula sobre bets no defeso eleitoral
item.description: The president of the TSE, Minister Nunes Marques, authorized the Lula government to disseminate institutional advertising about the risks of online betting during the electoral blackout period (July to October 2026). The campaign, named 'National Campaign for Prevention of Harms from Online Betting', aims to inform the public about mental health impacts and guide them on warning signs and SUS services. The minister emphasized there is no electoral intent, stating the action complies with the prohibition on abusive use of public resources.

item.title: Pesquisa interna do PL desanima grupo de Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio
item.description: Internal PL polls in Rio de Janeiro show Flávio Bolsonaro technically tied with Lula, raising concerns among party leaders, as the state is considered the historical heartland of bolsonarismo. The result is seen as a warning sign for the senator’s presidential campaign.

item.title: A multa que Flávio Bolsonaro terá de pagar caso carta do pai seja considerada irregular
item.description: The campaign of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) could face a fine of up to R$ 25,000 if the dissemination of a letter written by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is deemed premature electoral propaganda by the TSE. The minimum fine under electoral law is R$ 5,000. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Governo Lula avalia que tarifaço só será negociado após as eleições, caso taxa seja confirmada pelos EUA
item.description: The Lula administration believes that any potential U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods will only be negotiated after the 2026 elections, as the U.S. may wait to see whether Flávio Bolsonaro or Lula wins, given their diametrically opposed stances on trade concessions. The USTR decision could be announced starting this Wednesday, and the Planalto will await the list of affected products before crafting a response, avoiding premature actions. Flávio Bolsonaro’s request for a delay was seen as a move that benefits Lula’s position.

item.title: Após queixa de Alcolumbre, articuladores de Lula tentam conter Boulos e bancada do PT em embate sobre fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Lula’s political allies are attempting to contain pressure from Minister Guilherme Boulos and the PT caucus in the Chamber to vote on ending the 6x1 work schedule, following a formal complaint by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who opposes the proposal. The clash unfolds amid delicate political negotiations over labor reform, as the government seeks to avoid institutional rupture while keeping its base mobilized.

item.title: Rumble afirma que AGU mudou versão para defender Moraes
item.description: Rumble and Trump Media & Technology Group told a Florida court that the AGU changed its position on the reach of Brazilian judicial decisions by Minister Alexandre de Moraes to try to dismiss the case in the U.S. The companies claim that in June 2025, Brazil’s Justice Department told the U.S. Department of Justice that Brazilian rulings have effect only domestically and must be enforced via international cooperation channels, but now the AGU argues Moraes’ orders are sovereign acts immune from U.S. scrutiny. The suit does not challenge the validity of Moraes’ decisions in Brazil, but whether they can impose obligations on U.S. entities without U.S. government authorization or diplomatic mechanisms.

item.title: Após convencer Cid Gomes, PT busca alianças no Ceará e negocia 2ª vaga ao Senado, diante de disputa acirrada com Ciro
item.description: The PT in Ceará is seeking to define a second Senate candidate for Governor Elmano de Freitas's ticket, already confirmed with Cid Gomes (PSB), to strengthen the campaign amid a tight race against Ciro Gomes (PSDB). Names under discussion include Luizianne Lins (Rede), Eunício Oliveira (MDB), Chiquinho Feitosa (Republicanos), and potential PSD or PP representatives. Cid Gomes' candidacy was secured after a meeting with Lula, aiming to create a political counterpoint to Ciro and broaden state-level alliances.

item.title: Reuniões de madrugada, codinomes de heróis, dinheiro vivo: as provas que levaram a PF a indiciar 48 pessoas por fraude no INSS
item.description: The Federal Police indicted 48 individuals, including INSS employees, for a fraud scheme involving R$ 708 million in improper deductions from retirees' paychecks, featuring clandestine meetings, superhero codenames, and cash transactions. This case is part of a broader investigation into R$ 6.3 billion in alleged misappropriation, increasing pressure on President Lula’s administration during an election year. The report, delivered to the STF on Tuesday, is subscriber-only.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio quer adotar 'modo Bolsonaro' e replicar lives semanais
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign plans to adopt weekly live streams as a central tool to engage his Bolsonarist base, inspired by the model used by former President Jair Bolsonaro but adapted to his own style. The streams would be flexible, used to quickly respond to political events and maintain direct contact with supporters, as seen after the suspension of his visits to his father by the STF.

item.title: Sumiço de acervo em palácio de MG: quem pode ser responsabilizado?
item.description: The alleged disappearance of part of the Palácio das Mangabeiras' collection — including artworks, furniture, utensils, and a library of 1,038 restored books — is under investigation by the TCE-MG following a complaint by the ALMG. The Minas Gerais government claims the items were legally transferred, while former governor Romeu Zema dismissed the allegations, joking that savings from not occupying the palace would cover 'old furniture'. Lawyer Berlinque Cantelmo stated the collection is public property of the state, with the governor acting as administrator, not owner.

item.title: Sem comando de Michelle, mulheres do PL temem boicote a candidaturas
item.description: Women in the PL express concern over the lack of leadership in PL Women after Michelle Bolsonaro's departure, fearing that female candidacies for 2026 will be harmed by the interruption of her expansion plan, which aimed to allocate resources and structure to increase women's representation. Despite Valdemar Costa Neto's promises to follow through on Michelle's agreements, allies report uncertainty about the continuity of the candidate lists submitted by state leaders.

item.title: O plano de Flávio para as mulheres
item.description: Following attacks by Michelle Bolsonaro on Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's pre-campaign team mobilized to finalize the 'Brasil por Elas' initiative targeting women, part of the senator's government platform. The launch will feature a national tour with Flávio, his wife Fernanda, and female right-wing leaders.

item.title: Aliados apostam que Moraes vai rever veto à visita de Flávio ao pai
item.description: Allies of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes believe he will reverse the 90-day ban preventing Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, under house arrest. The July 13 decision was seen as excessive and emotionally driven, with critics in the STF and Lula government citing flawed reasoning. The measure bolsters Flávio’s narrative of victimhood, as he accuses Moraes of electoral interference.

item.title: Carta de Bolsonaro reacende debate sobre propaganda e ‘palavras mágicas’ no TSE
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's letter supporting Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) presidential candidacy reignited the debate over what constitutes premature electoral campaigning, after Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered the Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office to analyze the case. The subscriber-exclusive article highlights the tension between free speech and electoral regulations at the TSE.

item.title: Possibilidade de novo tarifaço de Trump vira cabo de guerra entre Lula e Flávio antes das eleições
item.description: The threat of Donald Trump imposing 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods has become a political flashpoint between the Lula government and pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, who traveled to the U.S. to urge delaying the decision until after the October elections. While the government pursues diplomatic solutions and accuses the Bolsonaro clan of harming exporters, Flávio argues that imposing tariffs now would be 'the worst possible moment' given potential political shifts post-election. The USTR is expected to finalize the decision this Wednesday following its Section 301 investigation.

item.title: A carta de Jair Bolsonaro aos brasileiros e os impactos políticos na candidatura de Flávio - O Assunto #1761
item.description: A letter written by Jair Bolsonaro during his house arrest was shared by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, in which the former president urged allies to unite and endorsed his son as the best option for the 2026 presidential race. The publication prompted Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to rule that Bolsonaro violated the ban on social media use, even through intermediaries, leading to a prohibition on father-son contact until after the first round of elections and an investigation into Flávio for premature campaigning.

item.title: EUA decidem nesta quarta sobre novas taxas ao Brasil; governo Lula aposta em prazo para decisão entrar em vigor e lista de exceções
item.description: The Lula government awaits a U.S. decision on potential tariffs of up to 25% on Brazilian goods, with the deadline set for Wednesday (15). Despite lacking official signals, it bets on a gradual implementation process and exceptions to reduce economic impact. The U.S. investigation cites illegal deforestation, piracy, and PIX use as trade-restricting practices by Brazil.

item.title: Flávio escolhe Carlos Portinho para vaga ao Senado pelo RJ
item.description: The PL has designated Senator Carlos Portinho as its pre-candidate for Senate re-election in Rio de Janeiro, ending internal uncertainties after Cláudio Castro withdrew due to ineligibility in the Master case. The decision was brokered by Flávio Bolsonaro, pre-candidate for President, in agreement with Jair Bolsonaro. Portinho, who has led the PL Senate bloc since assuming office in 2020, defeated federal deputy Carlos Jordy in the internal race, while Belford Roxo’s former mayor Márcio Canella was arrested for illegal firearm possession.

item.title: Preso, Lula recebeu Haddad semanalmente e orientou campanha em 2018 via cartas e recados
item.description: While imprisoned during Operation Car Wash, Lula received Fernando Haddad weekly until the start of the 2018 election runoff, directing campaign strategy through letters and political messages conveyed via allies.

item.title: A aliados, Valdemar minimiza bloqueio de bens e diz ver ação política
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL and under investigation by the Federal Police for illicit interference in parliamentary amendments, downplayed the R$119 million asset freeze ordered by Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino, claiming the decision is politically motivated. He has been speaking with São Paulo allies to reduce the perceived seriousness of the case.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio aposta em OAB para reaver visitas a Bolsonaro, mas admite pessimismo com Moraes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) pre-campaign is banking on an OAB request to overturn a ban imposed by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes that prohibits him from visiting his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for the next 90 days. Despite the legal push, Flávio's team admits pessimism about the likelihood of success given the minister's stance.

item.title: A direita está esfarelada
item.description: The text contrasts the historical fragmentation of the Brazilian left in the 20th century — exemplified by figures like Dilma Rousseff who passed through multiple clandestine organizations — with the current disintegration of the Brazilian right. It suggests that while the left once experienced deep divisions, it is now the right undergoing a process of organizational and ideological fragmentation. The analysis highlights a cyclical pattern of polarization and splintering in Brazil’s political landscape.

item.title: As pautas que vão decidir a eleição, segundo diretor do Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: Murilo Hidalgo, director of Paraná Pesquisas, states that the 90-day ban preventing Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former president Jair Bolsonaro may be used as a judicial persecution narrative in the campaign, but it will not be decisive for voters. He notes that recent polls show a balanced race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential second runoff, within the margin of error. The issues that will truly decide the election are the economy, public security, health, and voters’ wallets — not judiciary-related disputes.

item.title: Pesquisa: Kássio e eu no Sindicato dos Cabeçudos. Mas a dele está oca?
item.description: The author criticizes polling institutes for producing manipulated or biased numbers, especially when funded by parties or candidates, and rejects the idea of an 'accuracy seal' proposed by Kássio Nunes Marques, president of the TSE, as naive given the potential for methodological and intentional biases. He asserts that serious polls only reflect the current moment, not predict the future with certainty, and that distrust in the sector is justified by practices such as pre-set filters and covert advisory roles to candidates.

item.title: Os interesses escusos por trás das emendas parlamentares
item.description: Transparência Brasil reports that over R$1 billion in parliamentary committee amendments lack identified authors, as attribution is given only to party leaderships, preventing society from knowing who decides the allocation of funds. Executive director Juliana Sakai states this mechanism mirrors the unconstitutional 'secret budget,' undermining both transparency and the quality of public spending by diverting funds from structural projects to electoral interests.

item.title: ‘Pauta-bomba’: como votaram os senadores na aprovação da PEC dos agentes de saúde
item.description: The Senate approved the health agents' PEC, establishing special retirement for community health and endemic disease control workers, with 73 votes in favor and 1 against in both rounds. Labeled a 'bomb agenda' by the government due to its estimated R$ 27.9 billion impact over ten years, the Executive threatens to challenge it in the Supreme Court. Senators Flávio Bolsonaro, Izalci Lucas, Rogério Marinho, Daniella Ribeiro, and Teresa Leitão did not participate in either vote, while Hamilton Mourão was the sole dissenting vote.

item.title: Brasil chama tarifa dos EUA de ‘injusta’ em nova reunião
item.description: Brazil labeled as 'unjust' the potential imposition of new U.S. tariffs on national products during a high-level meeting with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, held on the eve of the deadline for the Trump administration's decision on surcharges. The government reiterated that USTR recommendations lack technical foundation and that imposing 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods or an additional 12.5% linked to forced labor investigations is not the path to a mutually suitable bilateral agreement.

item.title: Aprovação de 'pauta-bomba' no Senado é criticada por Renan Santos: 'sabotagem com o próximo governo'
item.description: The Senate approved a PEC creating special retirement benefits for community health agents and endemic disease fighters, with an estimated fiscal impact of R$27 billion over ten years. Despite the Lula government's opposition, the entire government coalition, including eight PT senators, voted in favor. Presidential pre-candidate Renan Santos (Missão) condemned the move as 'sabotage' against the next government, arguing the fiscal burden will fall on a future administration.

item.title: Voto feminino é vital para a democracia, ressalta Nelsinho Trad
item.description: Senator Nelsinho Trad (PSD-MS) stated that women's voting is vital for Brazilian democracy and criticized the notion that women should not vote or follow their husbands. He emphasized that women secured the right to vote nearly 100 years ago, now constitute half of the electorate, and head more than half of Brazilian households.

item.title: Paim defende novas fontes de financiamento para a Previdência
item.description: Senator Paulo Paim (PT-RS) criticized recent pension reforms focused on fiscal austerity, arguing they harm vulnerable workers and undermine the social security system as a tool for income distribution. He cited a Federal Revenue study showing a 56% loss in pension revenue due to tax evasion, delinquency, and fiscal renunciations, and endorsed PEC 1/2026, which would shift the basis for employer pension contributions from payroll to gross corporate revenue to relieve labor-intensive sectors and target high-profit industries. Paim also denounced pension privatization, citing its failure abroad and severe impoverishment of the elderly, insisting that dignified retirement is a matter of survival and social justice.

item.title: Cleitinho propõe debate sobre pena de morte
item.description: Senator Cleitinho (Republicanos-MG) advocated for reopening the debate on the death penalty in Brazil, citing the death of a 10-month-old child in Fortaleza with suspected sexual violence, and suggested the issue could only be addressed via a new constitution, as the current ban is a constitutional clause that cannot be amended except in war. He also reiterated his support for PEC 221/2019, which would abolish the 6x1 work schedule, comparing workers' long hours to legislators' lighter schedules due to recesses and election campaigns.

item.title: STF arquiva ação do PSOL contra Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Kassio Nunes Marques dismissed a criminal complaint filed by PSOL against Jair Bolsonaro related to the Covid-19 CPI. The ruling followed the Attorney General's Office opinion, which found no evidence of active corruption or administrative advocacy by the former president.

item.title: “Vamos examinar a base das tarifas e reagir”, diz Vieira sobre EUA
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated Brazil will wait for the official announcement of U.S. tariffs before responding, emphasizing ongoing negotiations. He noted that any reaction will depend on the measures' content and that Brazil has multiple response mechanisms, without specifying which. Vieira also highlighted the Canada agreement as part of Brazil's strategy to diversify trade partners, mentioning ties with the EU, U.S., China, Southeast Asia, and Africa.

item.title: Câmara aprova “filtro de relevância” para recursos ao STJ
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved Bill 3.085/2026, which establishes a 'relevance filter' for appeals to the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), requiring appellants to demonstrate social, economic, political, or legal impact for their case to be reviewed. The text, approved without changes from the Senate version, also allows for the suspension of up to six months of similar pending cases at the STJ. The bill now proceeds to presidential sanction or veto by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

item.title: Próteses do SUS são melhores que 'dentadura do Trump', diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that dental prostheses provided by Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) are superior to the 'denture' used by U.S. President Donald Trump. The remark was made during an event on Tuesday, the 14th, as part of an indirect critique of private healthcare and living standards in the United States.

item.title: Cuba sofre 3º apagão de energia em 9 dias, diz governo cubano
item.description: Cuba experienced its third nationwide blackout in nine days on Tuesday (Jul 14, 2026), due to an energy crisis worsened by fuel shortages and deteriorating infrastructure, according to the Cuban government. Meanwhile, Brazil sent its third humanitarian aid shipment in 2026, delivering 48 tons of powdered milk via the Brazilian Air Force, but reiterated it will not provide fuel or energy sector support to avoid U.S. sanctions.

item.title: Flávio anuncia Carlos Portinho como candidato ao Senado no RJ após operações contra Castro e Canella
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro announced Carlos Portinho as the bolsonarist candidate for the Rio de Janeiro Senate seat, replacing Cláudio Castro, who withdrew after becoming a target of a Federal Police operation. The announcement follows PF operations against Castro and Márcio Canella, both Bolsonaro allies, with Portinho having received Jair Bolsonaro’s endorsement and being described as a Senate government leader.

item.title: Flávio oficializa Carlos Portinho como pré-candidato ao Senado no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro officially announced Carlos Portinho as the PL party's pre-candidate for the Senate in Rio de Janeiro, stating that Jair Bolsonaro had already set his preference for Portinho. The announcement was made in a video released on Tuesday, the 14th, alongside the senator. The move reinforces Bolsonarista efforts to maintain political influence in the state.

item.title: Governo estuda reciprocidade contra tarifaço de Trump, e ministros levarão proposta a Lula
item.description: The Brazilian government is considering reciprocal measures in response to a potential new tariff increase by the United States against Brazilian products, should Donald Trump be elected in 2024. Ministers are expected to present a proposal to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for Brazil to impose equivalent tariffs on U.S. goods, aiming to protect domestic industry and ensure balance in trade relations.

item.title: Tarifaço pode levar Brasil a usar Lei da Reciprocidade, diz Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the Brazilian government is likely to resume the reciprocity process if the U.S. confirms new 25% tariffs on Brazilian exports, awaiting a final decision by July 15. The measure requires presidential approval and will be applied cautiously, while the MDIC continues talks with U.S. officials to avoid escalation. The economic team also considers issuing a new provisional measure to support affected sectors, modeled after the Brazil Soberano program.

item.title: TSE atualiza aplicativo e-Título e libera novas funcionalidades
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) updated the e-Título app with new features, including absence justification via geolocation on election day, document submission after the vote, payment of electoral fines via PIX or credit card through integration with PagTesouro, real-time tracking of requests, and issuance of party affiliation certificates for users with biometrics. The app is free for Android and iOS. The 2026 elections will have a first round on October 4 and a potential second round on October 25 for major offices.

item.title: Câmara aprova projeto que cria ‘filtro de relevância’ e limita recursos ao STJ
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved the bill establishing a 'relevance filter' for special appeals at the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), allowing the rapporteur to suspend proceedings for up to six months (renewable once) if the appeal demonstrates significant social, economic, political, or juridical impact. The proposal, already passed by the Senate, awaits President Lula’s sanction and aims to alleviate the STJ’s workload by focusing on cases of broader relevance, while preserving access to justice.

item.title: Em meio a novo atrito com Moraes, Jair Bolsonaro recebe uma boa notícia do STF
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Nunes Marques archived a 2021 criminal complaint against Jair Bolsonaro alleging administrative advocacy and active corruption, accepting the Prosecutor General's argument that the remarks were an informal, private conversation. The ruling comes amid renewed tensions with Minister Alexandre de Moraes, who recently restricted visits to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro remains under house arrest serving a 27-year-and-3-month sentence for his role in the coup plot.

item.title: PL escolhe Carlos Portinho como pré-candidato ao Senado no RJ
item.description: Senator Carlos Portinho (PL-RJ) has been confirmed as the PL’s pre-candidate for Senate re-election in Rio de Janeiro in 2026, following Flávio Bolsonaro’s endorsement. The decision resolves an internal party conflict after Portinho was initially sidelined in favor of Cláudio Castro and Márcio Canella. Portinho returns to the center of Bolsonarist mobilization in the state after Castro withdrew due to Federal Police investigations.

item.title: OAB dá' carteirada' de advogado pró-Flávio no caso da carta de Bolsonaro
item.description: The OAB issued a note requesting Minister Alexandre de Moraes to lift the contact ban between Flávio Bolsonaro and Jair Bolsonaro, but the move was deemed purely corporate and lacking legal significance.
